title: Forecasting as Rendering: A 2D Gaussian Splatting Framework for Time Series Forecasting

problem.claim: Time series forecasting is difficult because intra-period fluctuations and inter-period trends are intricately entangled.

gap.claim: Existing 2D period-phase representations suffer from topological mismatch caused by broken chronological continuity and inefficient fixed-size representations that lack adaptive resolution.

contributions.claim: TimeGS reframes time series forecasting as 2D generative rendering by modeling the future sequence as a latent 2D temporal surface.
The Multi-Basis Gaussian Kernel Generation block synthesizes Gaussian kernels from a fixed dictionary to stabilize optimization.
The Multi-Period Chronologically Continuous Rasterization block enforces temporal continuity across periodic boundaries.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe TimeGS as a novel framework that shifts forecasting from regression to 2D generative rendering.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on standard benchmark datasets are reported to show state-of-the-art or competitive performance.
The authors provide a code repository for TimeGS.

narrative_sequence.summary: Forecasting is challenging because temporal fluctuations and trends are entangled.
Prior 2D reshaping approaches introduce chronological discontinuities and inefficient fixed-resolution representations.
TimeGS recasts forecasting as rendering a latent 2D temporal surface with anisotropic Gaussian kernels.
MB-GKG stabilizes kernel generation, while MP-CCR preserves chronological continuity across periods.
The authors report competitive benchmark performance and provide code.

source_observation.claim: Fixed-size 2D representations may allocate capacity inefficiently for compressible, non-stationary temporal patterns.

interpretation.claim: Representation resolution should adapt to the local complexity of the data rather than remain uniformly fixed.

application.claim: Forecasting systems could benefit from geometrically adaptive representations that allocate modeling capacity according to temporal variation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when adaptive Gaussian representations outperform fixed-resolution alternatives.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, forecasting tasks, horizons, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide ablation results or implementation details beyond the two named blocks.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported performance.
